source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Monitor primarily for severe hypertension because the combination predictably increases systemic vascular resistance.","B":"Monitor for marked psychomotor stimulation because opioids reverse the sedating effects of gabapentin.","C":"Monitor for excessive sedation and respiratory depression because opioids can add to gabapentin-related central nervous system and respiratory depression.","D":"Monitor for serotonin syndrome because gabapentin acts as a strong serotonin reuptake inhibitor when combined with an opioid."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA warns that serious breathing difficulties can occur with gabapentin or pregabalin in patients with respiratory risk factors, including use of opioids and other CNS depressants. When co-prescribing, clinicians should use caution and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.8 — Respiratory Depression with CNS depressants including opioids. source_row.stem: A client taking gabapentin is newly prescribed an opioid. Which adverse effect is most important to monitor for when these medications are used together?
